log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Rotom
Floette used Light of Ruin → Tyranitar
Floette used Light of Ruin → Tyranitar

decisions.rationale: Lead Overqwil+Talonflame: Intimidate plus Poison Jab pressure Whimsicott, Quick Guard blocks Prankster Tailwind/Encore, and Talonflame can hit Gholdengo. Rotom-Wash is the defensive pivot: burns Tyranitar/Arcanine, checks Basculegion, and resists Make It Rain. Floette is kept back as the Mega cleaner for Tyranitar and Water-types once Gholdengo is gone.
decisions.notebook: Game1 core: Overqwil/Talonflame/Rotom/Floette; lead Overqwil/Talonflame. Whimsicott: Focus Sash survives one hit; Poison Jab leaves 1 HP, finish with Aqua Jet/Brave Bird; Overqwil immune Prankster status, Quick Guard blocks it. Gholdengo: Talonflame outspeeds and Flare Blitzes, Overqwil Crunches, Rotom resists Make It Rain; never expose Floette. Tyranitar: Intimidate and Rotom Will-O-Wisp; Floette Light of Ruin is the clean answer; protect Talonflame from Rock Slide. Milotic: avoid lowering its stats with Intimidate; Rotom Thunderbolt/Floette Energy Ball. Arcanine: Rotom Hydro/Will-O-Wisp, Talonflame resists Fire, Overqwil Intimidate. Basculegion: Rotom Thunderbolt/Floette Energy Ball/Overqwil Crunch; Quick Guard blocks Aqua Jet. Future games: if they spam Make It Rain/Rock Slide, consider Aegislash Wide Guard; if they drop Gholdengo or need Ground pressure, consider Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott enables immediate Prankster Tailwind and Encore, while Gholdengo applies strong spread pressure into the Fairy-heavy roster. Mega Tyranitar provides sand and Rock coverage against Talonflame, while Milotic is the reliable Garchomp check with Ice Beam and defensive recovery.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 team selection: default four are Whimsicott/Gholdengo lead with Mega Tyranitar and Milotic in back. Preserve Tailwind, use Gholdengo for immediate spread pressure, Mega Tyranitar for Talonflame pressure, and Milotic as the primary Garchomp response.

decisions.rationale: Talonflame always outspeeds Gholdengo (178 vs 104-136). Flare Blitz has ~70%+ OHKO chance; guaranteed if Helping Hand is active. Removing Gholdengo eliminates the Power Gem threat (191-275% on Talonflame). Overqwil Poison Jab breaks Whimsicott's Focus Sash (4x), setting up Aqua Jet priority finish next turn. Main risk: Gholdengo survives and Make It Rains (80-115% on Overqwil), but this is acceptable given the upside of removing both threats.
decisions.notebook: Game1 core: Overqwil/Talonflame/Rotom/Floette; lead Overqwil/Talonflame. Whimsicott: Focus Sash survives one hit; Poison Jab leaves 1 HP, finish with Aqua Jet/Brave Bird; Overqwil immune Prankster status, Quick Guard blocks it. Gholdengo: Talonflame outspeeds and Flare Blitzes (~70% OHKO, guaranteed with Helping Hand), Overqwil Crunches (same range); Power Gem guaranteed OHKO on Talonflame—never let Gholdengo move freely vs Talonflame; Make It Rain can OHKO Overqwil (80-115%), protect or switch if Gholdengo lives; Rotom resists Make It Rain; never expose Floette to Steel. Tyranitar: Intimidate and Rotom Will-O-Wisp; Floette Light of Ruin is the clean answer; protect Talonflame from Rock Slide. Milotic: avoid lowering its stats with Intimidate; Rotom Thunderbolt/Floette Energy Ball. Arcanine: Rotom Hydro/Will-O-Wisp, Talonflame resists Fire, Overqwil Intimidate. Basculegion: Rotom Thunderbolt/Floette Energy Ball/Overqwil Crunch; Quick Guard blocks Aqua Jet. Encore fails turn 1 (no prior move). Future games: if they spam Make It Rain/Rock Slide, consider Aegislash Wide Guard; if they drop Gholdengo or need Ground pressure, consider Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Do not concede. Replace Talonflame with Rotom-Wash: Make It Rain is 0.25x into Rotom but 2x into Floette, so Floette is unsafe against Gholdengo. Rotom also preserves a long-term answer to Tyranitar, Arcanine, and Basculegion. Overqwil stays active and can use Aqua Jet priority next turn if Whimsicott remains.
decisions.notebook: Game1 core: Overqwil/Talonflame/Rotom-Wash/Floette-Eternal; lead Overqwil/Talonflame. Whimsicott has Focus Sash and Prankster Tailwind/Encore; finish it with priority such as Aqua Jet after one hit. Overqwil is immune to Prankster status; Talonflame Quick Guard blocks Prankster moves. Gholdengo is Life Orb Modest with Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Power Gem/Protect; Rotom-Wash is the safe Make It Rain answer. Never switch Floette into Steel attacks. Overqwil Crunch is the main Overqwil pressure into Gholdengo but risky if Make It Rain is live. Tyranitar likely Mega with Sand Stream; soften with Intimidate/Will-O-Wisp, Floette Light of Ruin is the clean answer, protect Talonflame from Rock Slide. Milotic has Competitive: avoid lowering its stats; hit with Rotom Thunderbolt or Floette Energy Ball. Arcanine has Intimidate and Shuca Berry; Rotom Hydro Pump/Will-O-Wisp, Talonflame resists Fire. Basculegion has Adaptability; Rotom Thunderbolt, Floette Energy Ball, Overqwil Crunch; Quick Guard blocks Aqua Jet. Future games: consider Aegislash with Wide Guard if they spam Make It Rain/Rock Slide; consider Garchomp if Gholdengo is gone or Ground pressure is needed.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott safely establishes Tailwind before Talonflame, preserving speed control for the turn and subsequent turns. Gholdengo targets Talonflame with super-effective Power Gem; even through Charti Berry it has a meaningful OHKO range and immediately pressures the fastest opposing threat.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Tailwind as the primary speed-control plan. Gholdengo provides immediate spread or super-effective special pressure; Mega Tyranitar is the preferred later Mega against Talonflame, while Milotic is reserved as the main response to Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Make It Rain can OHKO Overqwil (80-115%), so Protect is essential. Rotom resists Make It Rain at 0.25x and is safe. Hydro Pump deals 46-84% to Gholdengo, putting it in KO range for next turn. Whimsicott at 1% is trivial to clean up later; risking Overqwil to Aqua Jet it is not worth the Make It Rain exposure.

decisions.rationale: Prankster Encore locks Overqwil into its revealed Poison Jab, which cannot affect Gholdengo. Gholdengo then uses spread Make It Rain for strong pressure on Overqwil and chip on Rotom-Wash while Whimsicott preserves the Tailwind advantage if it survives.
decisions.notebook: Tailwind is the primary speed-control plan. Gholdengo offers immediate spread and special pressure. Mega Tyranitar is the preferred later Mega against Talonflame; Milotic is reserved as the main response to Garchomp. Track revealed opposing sets, items, abilities, and move usage across games.

decisions.rationale: Aqua Jet (+1 priority) KOs 1% Whimsicott before it can Moonblast; only Helping Hand (+5) outruns it. Rotom Hydro Pump maximizes damage on Gholdengo (42-94%); even with Helping Hand, Gholdengo's -2 SpA Make It Rain only does 49-86% to Overqwil and 10-18% to Rotom—both survive. Priority on Whimsicott denies further Prankster utility.
decisions.notebook: Game1 core: Overqwil/Talonflame/Rotom-Wash/Floette-Eternal. Overqwil Dark typing grants immunity to Prankster status (Encore/Will-O-Wisp from Whimsicott). At -2 SpA, Gholdengo Make It Rain + Helping Hand does 49-86% to Overqwil and 10-18% to Rotom-Wash—not an OHKO on either. Hydro Pump (Mystic Water) deals 42-94% to Gholdengo; Thunderbolt only 29-65%. Whimsicott at 1% dies to any hit; Aqua Jet priority preempts Moonblast. Tyranitar likely Mega Sand Stream; Floette Light of Ruin is clean answer, protect Talonflame from Rock Slide. Milotic Competitive: avoid stat drops, hit with Rotom Thunderbolt/Floette Energy Ball. Arcanine Intimidate/Shuca: Rotom Hydro Pump/Will-O-Wisp. Basculegion Adaptability: Rotom Thunderbolt, Overqwil Crunch; Quick Guard blocks Aqua Jet. Future games: consider Aegislash Wide Guard for Make It Rain/Rock Slide spam; Garchomp if Ground pressure needed.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand amplifies Gholdengo’s Shadow Ball into Rotom-Wash, the only active foe not protected by Overqwil’s Encore lock. This preserves immediate pressure while Whimsicott can absorb a likely attack and be replaced by Milotic afterward.
decisions.notebook: Tailwind is the primary speed-control plan. Gholdengo provides immediate special pressure; Mega Tyranitar is preferred later against Talonflame, while Milotic is reserved for Garchomp. Revealed opposing information: Overqwil has Intimidate, Protect, Poison Jab, BlackGlasses, and Encore currently constrains its Protect; Rotom-Wash has Levitate, MysticWater, Hydro Pump, and Hydro Pump has missed once. Talonflame is fainted and its Charti Berry was consumed.

decisions.rationale: Switch Milotic in to trigger Competitive from Overqwil's Intimidate and preserve a strong answer to the remaining Ground threat; it also avoids exposing Tyranitar to Rotom-Wash's Water pressure. Keep Gholdengo in place.
decisions.notebook: Tailwind is the primary speed-control plan. Milotic is the preferred answer to Garchomp and benefits from Competitive when Overqwil's Intimidate activates. Tyranitar's Mega evolution is a later option for offensive pressure and sand support. Opponent facts: Overqwil has Intimidate, BlackGlasses, Protect, Poison Jab, Aqua Jet, and is constrained by Encore; Rotom-Wash has Levitate, MysticWater, Hydro Pump, and has missed once. Talonflame is fainted and its Charti Berry is consumed.

decisions.rationale: Aqua Jet (+1 priority) KOs Gholdengo at 6% HP (min roll 9.3% > 6% current) before it can attack Rotom under Tailwind. Thunderbolt is SE on Milotic for 45-95% chip. This removes Gholdengo safely and pressures Milotic. Rotom resists Milotic's STAB, so it survives any return hit.
decisions.notebook: Game1 core: Overqwil/Talonflame/Rotom-Wash/Floette-Eternal. Overqwil Dark typing grants immunity to Prankster status. Aqua Jet priority KO'd Gholdengo at 6%. Thunderbolt is primary Milotic answer (45-95%). Milotic Competitive: avoid stat drops, hit with Thunderbolt/Energy Ball. Tyranitar likely Mega Sand Stream; Floette Light of Ruin is clean answer. Arcanine Intimidate/Shuca: Rotom Hydro Pump/Will-O-Wisp. Basculegion Adaptability: Rotom Thunderbolt, Overqwil Crunch; Quick Guard blocks Aqua Jet. Future games: consider Aegislash Wide Guard for Make It Rain/Rock Slide spam; Garchomp if Ground pressure needed.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Gholdengo from Overqwil’s Encore-locked Aqua Jet and Rotom’s attacks while Milotic’s Competitive-boosted Ice Beam pressures Overqwil. With Tailwind, Milotic acts before Rotom but after Aqua Jet; this avoids risking an immediate Gholdengo loss while making progress.
decisions.notebook: Tailwind remains the primary speed-control plan. Milotic is the preferred answer to Garchomp and benefits from Competitive after Intimidate. Tyranitar’s Mega evolution is a later offensive and sand-support option. Preserve Gholdengo when possible because it provides important Steel/Ghost pressure; use Mega Tyranitar selectively rather than automatically.

decisions.rationale: Crunch OHKOs Gholdengo and Overqwil outspeeds it, so Aqua Jet's priority is unnecessary; Crunch also punishes Basculegion/Arcanine switches far better. Rotom's Thunderbolt KOes Milotic before it can move. This clears both active threats or forces bad Protect/switch guesses while keeping Floette intact.
decisions.notebook: Game1 core: Overqwil/Talonflame/Rotom-Wash/Floette-Eternal. Overqwil: Crunch is preferred over Aqua Jet into Gholdengo because it outspeeds and punishes Basculegion/Arcanine switches; Aqua Jet only for priority or Tyranitar chip. Black Glasses boosts Crunch. Rotom-Wash: Thunderbolt is the reliable Milotic answer; Hydro Pump hits Fire/Rock switch-ins but is inaccurate and weak into Water. Will-O-Wisp can neuter Arcanine/physical Tyranitar; Gholdengo is immune to status. Milotic Competitive: avoid stat drops; pressure with special attacks, especially Thunderbolt/Energy Ball. Floette-Eternal with Floettite/Light of Ruin is primary answer to Tyranitar and can use Energy Ball for Water/Rock. Tyranitar likely Mega sand; expect Rock Slide/Crunch/Ice Punch, use Rotom's bulk and Floette Fairy pressure. Arcanine Intimidate/Shuca: Rotom Hydro/Will-O-Wisp; Overqwil Crunch still chips after Intimidate. Basculegion Adaptability: Rotom Thunderbolt and Overqwil Crunch; Aqua Jet is poor into it. Future games: consider Aegislash Wide Guard for Make It Rain/Rock Slide spam; Garchomp if Ground pressure needed. Protect sequencing: repeated Protect success declines.

decisions.rationale: Protect Milotic from Rotom-Wash’s potentially lethal Thunderbolt while Gholdengo targets the weakened Rotom-Wash. Shadow Ball may KO; even if it falls short, preserving Milotic maintains the key Garchomp answer, while Gholdengo can be traded if necessary.
decisions.notebook: Tailwind is the primary speed-control plan. Milotic is the preferred answer to Garchomp and benefits from Competitive after Intimidate. Preserve Gholdengo when possible because it provides important Steel/Ghost pressure; use Mega Tyranitar selectively rather than automatically. Opposing revealed sets and items remain as recorded; hidden EVs and unrevealed Pokémon details must not be assumed.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Switch Overqwil to Floette: it outspeeds even Mega Tyranitar and Light of Ruin OHKOes Rock/Dark for 2x. Rotom Thunderbolts Milotic at 55%—the 45.5-95.3% range gives ~80% KO chance before Milotic can Recover. Opponent has no bench, so removing Milotic now is decisive. Floette at full HP comfortably tanks any Rock Slide on the switch-in.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Eternal (Floettite) can Mega Evolve and is the primary Tyranitar answer: Light of Ruin OHKOes Rock/Dark for 2x and Floette outspeeds Mega Tyranitar. Light of Ruin is 90% accurate with recoil equal to half damage dealt; Moonblast is the safer Fairy option. Rotom-Wash: Thunderbolt is the reliable Milotic KO; Hydro Pump hits Fire/Rock switch-ins but is inaccurate and weak vs Water; Will-O-Wisp neuters physical attackers (Arcanine, Tyranitar) but Gholdengo is immune to status. Milotic is Competitive—avoid stat drops, pressure with special attacks. Opposing Tyranitar is likely Mega Sand Stream with spread Rock Slide; shield frail allies or answer with Fairy. Overqwil: Black Glasses Crunch for chip; Aqua Jet priority only for Tyranitar/finishing. Future games: Aegislash Wide Guard covers Make It Rain/Rock Slide spam; Garchomp for Ground pressure. Repeated Protect success declines.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Recover preserves Milotic through the likely Thunderbolt while Mega Rock Slide pressures both foes and has a strong chance to remove Rotom-Wash, the immediate threat. Mega Tyranitar should survive priority Aqua Jet and likely Hydro Pump long enough to attack.
decisions.notebook: Milotic remains the preferred Garchomp answer and should generally be preserved. Tailwind is the primary speed-control plan when Whimsicott is available. Preserve Gholdengo when possible for Steel/Ghost pressure; Mega Tyranitar should be used selectively rather than automatically.

selection: Light of Ruin -> foe 2 (Tyranitar-Mega) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Tyranitar-Mega is the last foe—KO wins game 1. Mega Floette (SpA 227, Fairy Aura) Light of Ruin deals 81-171%; Aqua Jet adds 13-26%. Combined min ~94%, likely KO. Both outspeed (Floette 154 vs Ttar max 123). Moonblast too weak to reliably finish. Accept 90% acc for the KO shot.
decisions.notebook: Opponent game-1 team: Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Tyranitar/Milotic brought; Arcanine & Basculegion benched. Mega Floette-Eternal (Floettite): base 155 SpA, Fairy Aura, Speed 102; my spread 32SpA/32Spe/2HP → SpA 227, Spe 154. Light of Ruin 140BP/90acc/50% recoil; Moonblast safer. Overqwil Aqua Jet priority key for finishing. Tyranitar-Mega Adamant, Rock Slide/Crunch/Ice Punch/Protect, weak to Fairy/Water/Grass. Sandstorm active boosts Ttar SpD. Future: Aegislash Wide Guard vs Make It Rain/Rock Slide; Garchomp Ground pressure. Repeated Protect success declines.

decisions.rationale: Milotic is already fainted, so pass. Protect is essential: Floette moves before Tyranitar and threatens super-effective Fairy damage, while Overqwil's priority Aqua Jet is also super-effective. Rock Slide cannot KO either target and exposes Tyranitar to both attacks; sand chip may improve the next turn.
decisions.notebook: Milotic remains the preferred Garchomp answer and should generally be preserved when available. Tailwind is the primary speed-control plan when Whimsicott is available. Preserve Gholdengo when possible for Steel/Ghost pressure. Use Mega Tyranitar selectively rather than automatically, especially against strong Fairy- or Water-type pressure.

decisions.rationale: Tyranitar-Mega is the last foe. Aqua Jet (priority) chips 12-26%, then LoR hits for 81-171% SE with Fairy Aura—combined 94-198% likely KOs through sand SpD boost. 90% acc is worth it; even on miss, Overqwil (61%) survives any -1 Ttar hit and wins the 1v1 with repeated Aqua Jets. Moonblast+Aqua Jet only reaches 69-143%, too likely to leave Ttar standing.
decisions.notebook: Opponent game-1 roster: Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash, Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast/Helping Hand, Timid), Gholdengo (Life Orb, Modest, Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Power Gem/Protect), Tyranitar-Mega (Adamant, Rock Slide/Crunch/Ice Punch/Protect), Milotic (Bold, Leftovers, Competitive, Scald/Ice Beam/Recover/Protect). Benched: Arcanine (Jolly, Shuca Berry, Intimidate, Flare Blitz/Snarl/Extreme Speed/Protect), Basculegion (Adamant, Mystic Water, Adaptability, Wave Crash/Aqua Jet/Icy Wind/Protect). Key threats for future games: Gholdengo Make It Rain under Tailwind, Tyranitar sand + Rock Slide spread, Milotic Competitive punishing Intimidate. My team notes: Floette-Mega (Modest, Fairy Aura, 227 SpA, 154 Spe) has Light of Ruin (140BP/90acc/50% recoil) and Moonblast; Overqwil (Adamant, Intimidate, Black Glasses, 183 Atk, 137 Spe) has Aqua Jet priority. Rotom-Wash (Modest, Levitate, Mystic Water) provides Electric/Water coverage. Talonflame (Adamant, Gale Wings, Charti Berry) has Tailwind/Brave Bird/Flare Blitz/Quick Guard. Strategy: Use Intimidate to weaken physical attackers; Floette is primary special sweeper with Fairy Aura; Overqwil Aqua Jet is key priority finisher. Watch for Protect chains (success rate declines). Sand boosts Tyranitar SpD—need strong SE hits. Future draft considerations: Aegislash Wide Guard blocks Rock Slide/Make It Rain; Garchomp provides Ground pressure vs Tyranitar.

decisions.rationale: Rock Slide is the strongest immediate line: it pressures both foes and has a realistic chance to KO Floette-Mega despite spread reduction, while also chipping Overqwil. Protect is weakened and leaves Tyranitar exposed to their faster attacks without improving the board.
decisions.notebook: Milotic remains the preferred Garchomp answer and should be preserved when available. Tailwind is the primary speed-control plan when Whimsicott is available. Preserve Gholdengo where possible for Steel/Ghost pressure. Use Mega Tyranitar selectively rather than automatically, especially against strong Fairy- or Water-type pressure.

decisions.rationale: Floette fainted, must pass. Overqwil vs Tyranitar 1v1: Aqua Jet is priority +1 and 2x SE, dealing 12.6-26.3% (no KO from 79%). Protect only delays the inevitable since Rock Slide (21.9-43.8%) can still KO Overqwil at 27% next turn. Aqua Jet at least chips Tyranitar and retains ~30% survival chance via Rock Slide miss (10%) or low damage roll. Best line is priority Aqua Jet.

Future draft: Aegislash Wide Guard blocks Rock Slide/Make It Rain; Garchomp Ground pressure vs Tyranitar. Game 1 likely lost in 1v1 Overqwil vs Tyranitar; focus on game 2 adjustments.

decisions.rationale: Milotic is fainted, so only Tyranitar can act. Rock Slide offers the best chance to KO Overqwil despite its spread reduction and 90% accuracy, while Crunch cannot KO and Ice Punch is less powerful. The foe’s other active slot is already fainted.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Milotic as the preferred Garchomp answer when available. Use Tailwind as the primary speed-control plan when Whimsicott is available. Preserve Gholdengo for Steel/Ghost pressure where possible. Use Mega Tyranitar selectively rather than automatically, especially into strong Fairy- or Water-type pressure.
